title: step-n-substitution-rule
description: A formal closure-rule object that captures a step-n substitution recurrence: its antecedent is a conjunction of predicates over the prior n settled stages and its consequent produces new cell content at the next stage by an n-term recurrence, generated by formalizing a step-n-substitution-recurrence as a closure rule.

step.description: the look-back parameter n; the antecedent depends on the prior n settled stages

antecedent.description: the conjoined look-back predicates phi_i on cell-content at stage k - i, for i = 1..n

consequent.description: the constraint psi on cell-content at the next stage k + 1

substitutionMatrix.description: the associated n x n nonnegative-integer matrix M with M_ij the count of j-letters produced from an i-letter; distinct matrices at the same n give distinct rules

entries.description: the matrix rows over the naturals

growthRate.description: the dominant Perron-Frobenius eigenvalue of M; a degree-n algebraic number for primitive matrices

closureOrdinal.description: the substitution does not stabilize at any countable ordinal; new cells appear at every stage (aperiodic regime when E = omega_1)

scottContinuousAlone.description: the rule by itself depends on finitely many prior stages and is Scott-continuous; combined with limit-aggregation it becomes non-Scott-continuous
